_comment_bootstrap_sha: ONE-SHOT (ADR-1151). The fork has never released, so release-please has no previous tag to walk back to; this pins the commit-scan floor for the first cut only. scripts/release/rollover-changelog-fragments.sh deletes it in the release-merge PR, and the release-script-contract gate refuses to let it return once the manifest reaches 1.0.0.

.._comment_release_as: ONE-SHOT (ADR-1151, retargeted by ADR-1201 to the rc line). Forces the fork's FIRST release onto a fresh 1.0.0 number line; every vX.Y.Z tag currently reachable belongs to Netflix upstream history. release-as is a persistent, DEPRECATED override applied after commit analysis, so leaving it in place would pin every future release: scripts/release/rollover-changelog-fragments.sh deletes it in the release-merge PR and the release-script-contract gate refuses to let it return once the manifest reaches 1.0.0. Use a `Release-As: X.Y.Z` commit footer for any later forced version.
.._comment_prerelease: ADR-1201. The fork cuts release candidates before the final 1.0.0, so release-please publishes prereleases and GitHub marks them as such. `prerelease-type` fixes the channel at `rc`, matching the narrow tag pattern scripts/release/verify-release-version.sh accepts (vX.Y.Z-rc.N, no other identifier). Flip `prerelease` to false and set `release-as` to 1.0.0 for the final cut; the release-script-contract gate then starts enforcing removal of the one-shot fields, which it deliberately does NOT do while the manifest carries a prerelease suffix.
